messages.content: Implement a Python function from a JSON behavioral card. The card is the only task specification. Return a JSON object with a single string field code containing executable Python source. Define solve with the card's exact signature. Use only Python's standard library. Allowed imports: math, itertools, functools, collections, heapq, bisect, statistics, fractions, operator, typing. Do not import or call NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX or any other third-party library. Do not read files, use network, introspection, eval, exec, input or print. Implement computations yourself using built-ins and the allowed standard library. Return plain JSON-compatible values, not iterators or sets; use string keys in dictionaries. Include any helper functions in the code. No tests or main block. Raise ValueError where the card requires it.

Implement this card:
{
  "algorithm": [
    "Use Dijkstra's algorithm if method is 'dijkstra'",
    "Use Bellman-Ford algorithm if method is 'bellman-ford'",
    "Default to Dijkstra's algorithm if method is not specified"
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "Edges are distinct and form a simple undirected unweighted graph",
    "Vertices are numbered 0 to n-1",
    "source and target are valid vertices",
    "If method is not specified, default to Dijkstra's algorithm",
    "If weight is not specified, assume weight is 1"
  ],
  "edge_cases": [
    "source == target returns 0",
    "No path exists between source and target, raises ValueError",
    "Graph is disconnected, returns None or raises ValueError"
  ],
  "inputs": "n is an integer >= 1; edges is a list of distinct [u, v] pairs with 0 <= u < v < n; source and target are valid vertices.",
  "method_id": "networkx.shortest_path_length",
  "output": "Integer shortest-path length; raises ValueError if no path exists.",
  "purpose": "Compute the shortest path length in a graph with specified source and target nodes.",
  "signature": "solve(n, edges, source, target)"
}
